# The coupling contract

External models communicate with `landisR` through `landis_update()` and
`landis_apply()`.

A modifier is optional. A complete disturbance extension can generate the same
update directly.

# Discover capabilities

```{r capabilities}
caps <- landis_capabilities(sim)

caps

landis_supports(
  caps,
  c(
    "state.cohorts",
    "update.cohorts"
  )
)
```

Capabilities make engine-specific assumptions explicit.

For example, the current Biomass 5.2 engine advertises
`engine_input.sep`, whereas a future growth engine does not have to.

# A lightweight modifier

```{r modifier}
biotic_process <- landis_modifier(
  name = "biotic_process",
  state = "biomass",
  scope = "cell",
  requires = c(
    "state.biomass",
    "update.dynamic",
    "engine_input.sep"
  ),
  fun = function(state, inputs, context) {

    new_dynamic <- inputs$dynamic

    # User-defined scientific logic.
    # Nothing in landisR assumes that this is competition,
    # facilitation, fire, or any other specific process.

    landis_update(
      dynamic = new_dynamic,
      dynamic_mode = "replace"
    )
  }
)

sim <- landis_apply(
  sim,
  biotic_process
)
```

# Conditional no-op

A modifier can return `NULL` when nothing happens.

```{r no-op}
conditional_process <- landis_modifier(
  name = "conditional_process",
  state = "compact",
  fun = function(context) {

    if (context$year < 50) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    landis_update(
      metadata = list(
        triggered = TRUE
      )
    )
  }
)
```

# A full extension without landis_modifier()

A disturbance package does not need the modifier wrapper.

```{r extension}
result <- myFirePackage::run(
  model = fire_model,
  forest = landis_state(
    sim,
    representation = "cohorts"
  ),
  landscape = sim$project$canonical$landscape$cells,
  year = sim$year
)

sim <- landis_apply(
  sim,
  result
)
```

The extension only needs to return a valid `landis_update`.

# A plain function also works

```{r plain-function}
external_process <- function(simulation) {

  forest <- landis_state(
    simulation,
    representation = "cohorts",
    cells = selected_cells
  )

  # Arbitrary external calculations.

  landis_update(
    cohorts = forest
  )
}

sim <- landis_apply(
  sim,
  external_process
)
```

# Why this matters for future growth engines

The public coupling contract is not tied to Biomass Succession 5.2.

A future PnET-style engine can advertise a different capability set while fire,
harvest, insects, or other models continue communicating through
`landis_update()`.
